scope: selected current_dev; 60 problems x 3 paired seeds per method/objective
policy: Correction to the existing valid-output criterion; solver convergence is recorded separately. No solver, input, candidate or validation artifact is changed.
acceptance: Each attempt independently requires legal original input, exact saved request/input identity, receipt-bound formal candidate and passing independent validation, process exit 0, timed_out false, no exception, and cold end-to-end time within its original declared budget (60 seconds here). Missing historical fields are not inferred. The same minimum requirements apply to raw successes. Numeric candidate archives are reconstructed by the common CPU sampler and matched to saved q/time/segment, fixed endpoints, costs/duration, joint/motion limits and saved collision masks/clearances; numerical summaries must be consistent. No new GPU collision query is performed.
selection: Primary comparison still uses the first terminal attempt, never best-of retries. Dataset witnesses may establish numerical path existence from another valid attempt without increasing primary scores.

verified_findings: Supported finite candidate arrays reconstruct the saved q/time/segment and objective under the common sampler.

Unsealed, mismatching, missing, malformed, late, timed-out and exceptional output cannot be upgraded to success.
Finite region_residual must agree with the original common-validation tolerance; no geometry rerun is claimed.
Recorded external timeout/late completion has status precedence over solver_failed; raw status is retained.
Primary scores still select the first terminal attempt; a later accepted attempt can establish dataset feasibility existence without replacing that score.
limits: This checks saved collision evidence and coefficient/sample consistency; it does not repeat GPU/Drake collision geometry or establish continuous collision freedom.
Passing adversarial tests does not prove absence of every possible metadata/runtime failure.
Existing runtime and all historical artifacts remain unchanged; only derived indexing semantics are proposed.
